units: USD millions; growth rates are decimal fractions
status: Working analyst scenarios for review, not guidance, probabilities or a final valuation

Q26.locators: Note 18 segment revenue; MD&A launch metrics, Neutron timing and backlog

RELEASE26.locators: Third Quarter 2026 Guidance and business update

facts.backlog_note: Rounded segment totals differ by 0.1 from rounded total; do not plug either segment. Backlog is not cash or a dated revenue schedule; excludes unexercised options.
facts.revenue_metric_note: Launch count multiplied by the launch-price KPI is not GAAP segment revenue because recognition timing and other launch services differ.

management_guidance.neutron_timing: Q4 2026 pad-delivery target; not a guaranteed revenue launch date.

scope.owned_business: Rocket Lab including already acquired GEOST, Mynaric and Motiv; no separate extra revenue added for the same acquired businesses.
scope.iridium: Excluded from these standalone scenarios together with acquisition financing/consideration; no combined-company market-price conclusion permitted without a transaction case or explicit deferral condition.
scope.future_acquisitions: No additional acquisition growth or purchase consideration assumed.
scope.neutron: No separately added Neutron service revenue in 2026. After 2026 the model adds incremental Neutron revenue separately to the continuing launch pool. This is an analytical split, not a separately reported segment.
scope.valuation_timing: FY2026 includes actual H1 and estimated H2. Final DCF must value only cash flows after September 10; never discount the entire FY2026 cash flow on top of a September cash estimate.

downside.name: Delivery delays and slow Neutron qualification
downside.causal_story: Q3 misses guidance; space-program delivery slips, launch growth slows, and meaningful Neutron revenue starts in 2029. Cost integration must retain delay-related R&D and fixed costs rather than automatically reducing them with revenue.

base.name: Backlog execution and gradual Neutron ramp
base.causal_story: Q3 meets the guidance midpoint, Q4 advances with deliveries, space growth slows as scale rises, and incremental Neutron service revenue begins in 2027. Requires repeat orders, technical progress and funded capacity.

upside.name: Faster deliveries and successful launch expansion
upside.causal_story: Q3 reaches guidance high end and subsequent execution accelerates. Higher production, working capital and investment must be funded; this is not cost-free growth.

driver_challenges.basis: Base 257.5 is the 250-265 management-guidance midpoint; upside 265 is its upper end; downside 240 deliberately tests a miss.
driver_challenges.challenge: Guidance can miss; no Q3 reported result was public in the reviewed cutoff evidence.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Pre-cutoff guidance revision or independently dated delivery evidence; later actual results are monitoring evidence, not inputs to this historical valuation.

driver_challenges.basis: Analyst segment allocations; base 57.5/65 bracket H1 quarterly launch average 54.1245 and allow stronger second-half mix. Space revenue is total minus launch.
driver_challenges.challenge: Company did not guide segment revenue; HASTE timing prevents launch count times price from being an exact revenue formula.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Contract milestone recognition, launch-service mix and segment disclosure consistent with the cutoff.

driver_challenges.basis: Analyst delivery scenarios: base 280 is 8.74% above base Q3; downside flat at 240; upside 310 is 16.98% above upside Q3. No company Q4 guidance claimed.
driver_challenges.challenge: Backlog does not establish delivery dates, acceptance, margins or cash collection.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Funded delivery schedule and customer acceptance milestones supporting the assumed quarterly recognition.

driver_challenges.basis: Analyst 5%-20% annual growth envelope; base decelerates 15/12/10/8%. Capacity and mix improvement must support it. Incremental Neutron is excluded from this growth series.
driver_challenges.challenge: Manufacturing, launch-site or customer delays can prevent growth; price and recognized revenue vary by mission.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Vehicle build rate, reliable launch cadence, funded service contracts and revenue recognition schedules.

driver_challenges.basis: Analyst growth paths taper from 12/25/35% to 6/15/20% in downside/base/upside. Backlog supports demand context but does not mathematically establish these rates.
driver_challenges.challenge: H1 growth includes acquisitions; it cannot be extrapolated as organic growth. Future revenue exceeds current backlog and needs new orders and capacity.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Order replenishment, customer funding, contract completion estimates and segment production capacity.

driver_challenges.basis: Analyst ramp of recognized service equivalents, not a company launch manifest or a guaranteed mission count. Base 0/1/3/6/10; delayed 0/0/0/1/3; faster 0/2/5/10/16.
driver_challenges.challenge: Pad delivery is not first-flight success or commercial cadence. Over-time accounting can separate revenue from flight dates.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Qualification, first-flight success, funded manifests and production readiness, with consistent recognition policy.

driver_challenges.basis: Analyst scale assumption of 45/50/55 million per recognized service equivalent. No independently verified contracted ASP is claimed; do not infer the value from a bundled launch-plus-spacecraft award.
driver_challenges.challenge: Pricing, discounts, allocations and service scope can differ materially. This is a weakly evidenced driver requiring wide challenge.
driver_challenges.change_evidence: Pre-cutoff executed contract pricing and allocated performance obligations; otherwise retain explicit uncertainty and test removal of the Neutron ramp.
